explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The statement is a naturality property of two definitions that belong to the library itself, not to Mathlib: `ptOfHom` (a map X ⟶ Spec K becomes a convolution-wrapped ℤ-algebra hom K →ₐ[ℤ] Γ(X, ⊤)) and `postcomp` (composition with an algebra hom, as a monoid hom on `WithConv`). The proof is a short unfolding that rewrites with the library's own `ringHomOfHom_comp`. That lemma in turn follows from associativity of composition and the definitions of `Scheme.appTop` and `Scheme.Γ.map`. Mathlib supplies only the underlying ingredients (`Scheme.ΓSpecIso`, `appTop`, `Scheme.Γ_map_op`), and none of them states this result about `WithConv` algebra homs. All of the mathematical content sits in the library's own definitions, so there is nothing in Mathlib to call a duplicate or a special case. I read the definitions of `ptOfHom`, `postcomp` and `ringHomOfHom` in the library file.
